lens: code correctness, deterministic replay integrity, and Opik lifecycle auditability

findings.observation: The Opik-capable CLI still treats agent-definition digest as optional and falls back to a digest derived only from definitionId, version, and gitSha, so remote experiment identity can degrade to an operator-supplied surrogate instead of an immutable agent artifact digest.
findings.evidence: apps/eval-runner/src/cli.ts:89-109 requires --agent-definition-id and --agent-definition-version for Opik but not --agent-definition-digest, then synthesizes contentDigest with digestCanonicalJson({ definitionId, version, gitSha }); a real replay command on 2026-08-31, `pnpm --filter @talent-signal/eval-runner replay -- --id TS-TRJ-005 --artifact-dir <tmp>`, produced manifest.attempt.agentDefinition { definitionId: "evaluation-runner-control-plane", version: "0.1.0", contentDigest: "sha256:621e794f3a9751a07499c86dee4b8568e062a96db127a82d5a77d0f08c154383" }, exactly matching that fallback formula.
findings.user_impact: If an operator omits --agent-definition-digest during Opik projection, distinct agent configurations that share the same ID, version, and git SHA can be recorded as the same remote identity even though the transport now separates experiments by digest.
findings.recommendation: Require --agent-definition-digest whenever --opik is set, or source the digest from an immutable agent-definition artifact instead of synthesizing it at the CLI boundary.
findings.verification: Run `pnpm --filter @talent-signal/eval-runner replay -- --id TS-TRJ-005 --opik --agent-definition-id demo --agent-definition-version 1.0.0` and require an immediate local validation error until a SHA-256 --agent-definition-digest is supplied.

findings.observation: The machine validator still accepts a non-final cleanup state and does not bind the proof's claimed deletion target IDs back to checked artifacts, so part of the final deletion/cleanup story remains self-reported.
findings.evidence: scripts/evals/validate-evaluation-platform-proof.mjs:143-152 validates only deletion receipt digest, projectionId, status, readBackVerified, scope, retained surfaces, and reasonCode; it never checks docs/evaluations/2026-09-01-evaluation-platform/opik-integration-proof.json:143-146 externalTraceId, experimentId, or experimentItemId against a ledger event or receipt. The same validator also accepts proof.cleanup.taskOwnedLocalOpikStack of either "pending_final_independent_review" or "completed" at scripts/evals/validate-evaluation-platform-proof.mjs:166-169 while the shipped proof still records "pending_final_independent_review" at opik-integration-proof.json:179-183.
findings.user_impact: A proof can pass validation while the exact remote IDs said to be deleted are not independently rebound to the checked evidence, and while local task-owned cleanup is still marked pending rather than complete.
findings.recommendation: Extend the validator to compare proof.deletion externalTraceId, experimentId, and experimentItemId against the already-loaded v2 ledger completion event or a richer deletion receipt, and require cleanup.taskOwnedLocalOpikStack to be "completed" for a final proof artifact.
findings.verification: Mutate a copy of opik-integration-proof.json so the deletion IDs disagree with the v2 ledger or cleanup.taskOwnedLocalOpikStack stays pending, then require `node scripts/evals/validate-evaluation-platform-proof.mjs` to fail on that copy.

strengths: The first-round determinism break is genuinely closed: apps/eval-runner/src/cli.ts:176-232 and apps/eval-runner/src/runSuite.ts:197-206 now inject profile runtime into the real replay path, and two 2026-08-31 CLI reruns of `pnpm --filter @talent-signal/eval-runner replay -- --id TS-TRJ-005` produced identical runId, attemptId, manifestDigest, resultDigest, gateDigest, localArtifactDigest, outputDigest, startedAt, completedAt, and receiptDigest.

Pre-side-effect validation now happens before local writes: apps/eval-runner/src/runSuite.ts:197-198 validates profile compatibility and system-under-test before manifest persistence at 221-222, and a real incompatible-profile run of `pnpm --filter @talent-signal/eval-runner replay -- --id TS-TRJ-005 --profile memory-replay-v1 --artifact-dir <tmp>` exited 1 with `Scenario TS-TRJ-005 does not admit profile memory-replay-v1` and left no output directory.

The Opik lifecycle evidence is materially tighter: apps/eval-runner/src/opik/opikReporter.ts:82-123 requires the completed local artifact digest before projection; apps/eval-runner/src/projectionLedger.ts:156 maps receipt.localArtifactDigest from the ledger event; apps/eval-runner/src/opik/opikTransport.ts:276-326 enforces dataset-version and digest-bound experiment identity plus experiment-link readback; apps/eval-runner/src/opik/opikReporter.ts:235-285 and the checked ledger/receipt under projection-ledger-final-v2 prove trace-plus-experiment-link deletion readback.
missing_evidence: There is still no automated test that drives SdkOpikTransport.beginProjection through an existing same-name remote experiment whose metadata digests mismatch; apps/eval-runner/src/opik/opikTransport.test.ts:41-58 covers only the pure identity helper, not the remote reuse rejection path.

There is still no machine-checked negative test for the proof validator itself covering deletion-ID mismatch or pending cleanup acceptance; the current validator run only proves the shipped proof passes.
open_questions: Should Opik projection be allowed at all without an immutable agent-definition artifact digest, or is the product intent that every projected experiment be digest-bound end to end at the CLI boundary?
Do we want a separate intermediate proof state for local-stack cleanup, instead of allowing a file named as the final integration proof to validate while cleanup remains pending?
